statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. NQ is 29,373.00, +0.40%, 1.75 points below a 29,374.75 session high, having extended the post-halt reopen range to 29,247.75-29,374.75 without returning to the low. That unretraced overnight leg is a genuine directional signal and lifts Tail from 16 to 18, but it spans only 0.43% in thin post-close liquidity and arrives with implied volatility decaying, so it stays inside the low band. Stress holds at 72 because the 10-year closed at 5.01%, the top of its 4.94-5.01 day range, and the 2-year at 4.736% sits 0.6 basis points under its 52-week high.
recommendation: Tail rises on observed structure rather than assumption. The prior hour's 40.75-point reopen band has become a 127-point extension with the 29,247.75 low untested, which is the shallow-pullback signature that matters to a mean-reversion basket, so Tail steps from 16 to 18. Three considerations keep it well inside the low band: the move spans 0.43% and recovers a Fed-hike selloff rather than establishing a fresh trend, implied volatility decayed from an 18.94 session high to a 17.71 close, and cross-assets are not aligned behind it, with the Dow down 1.21% against a Nasdaq-100 cash close of +0.02% and crude 3.2% lower on reported progress restarting the damaged Saudi East-West pipeline. Stress stays in the high band on an unresolved front end: a 5.01% 10-year at its day high, a 2-year pinned near its 52-week high, and projections pointing to at least one further hike this year. The declared danger window remains the 13:30-14:30 UTC cash open on September 17, the first full regular session after the policy shift and the point at which persistent one-way structure would establish if it is going to. Tail remains well below the block threshold across the whole forecast.
headline: NQ grinds to 29,373.00 at its overnight high after the Fed's first hike in three years, lifting Tail to 18 inside the low band while a 5.01% 10-year keeps Stress high
body: The FOMC raised the federal funds target range by 25 basis points to 3-3/4 to 4 percent at 18:00 UTC in a unanimous 12-0 vote, the first increase in three years, stating that inflation remains elevated and that the action supports a timelier return to the Committee's 2 percent goal. The Summary of Economic Projections showed most participants expecting at least one further 25 basis point increase before year-end. Cash markets closed split: the Dow fell 631.21 points or 1.21% to 51,461.90, the S&P 500 lost 0.45% to 7,551.81, the Nasdaq Composite was effectively flat at 25,978.42, and the Nasdaq-100 closed 0.02% higher at 28,945.06 after traversing a 482-point intraday range of 28,753.29 to 29,235.89. The new evidence for this hour is the overnight tape. Where the previous assessment observed a contained 40.75-point reopen band, NQ has since worked up to 29,373.00, plus 116.25 points or 0.40% against a 29,256.75 prior close, and sits 1.75 points under the 29,374.75 session high as of 23:15 UTC. The 29,247.75 reopen low has not been revisited, so the overnight leg is directionally efficient and price is holding at its extreme. That is the structure that matters most to a mean-reversion basket, and it is the reason Tail steps up. The step is deliberately small. The entire extension spans 127 points, about 0.43%, in the thinnest liquidity of the twenty-four hour cycle, and its character is recovery of a policy-driven selloff rather than the start of a fresh trend. Implied volatility is decaying, with the VIX closing at 17.71 after an 18.94 session high and a 16.40 low. Cross-assets do not corroborate a directional equity path: crude settled about 3.2% lower near $102.43 with Brent down 2.7% to $105.83, after U.S. officials said the Saudi East-West pipeline damaged by drone strikes on September 10 would restart within days, a timeline independent analysts dispute in favour of weeks. Latest-session breadth context is split rather than aligned, with semiconductors mostly higher and megacap software lower. What keeps Stress high is the rates picture. The 10-year closed at 5.01%, the top of its 4.94 to 5.01 range and its highest since 2007, while the 2-year at 4.736% sits 0.6 basis points below a 4.742% 52-week high after trading as low as 4.602% intraday. A front end pinned at its highs with a further hike in the projections leaves long-duration technology exposed to any renewed repricing, which is the mechanism behind the elevated Stress reading even as Tail sits in the low band. The forecast opens at 18 for the current hour, the only slot backed by observed structure, holds 16 to 18 through the Asian session, and firms to 18 to 19 across the European morning and U.S. pre-market. It enters the watch band at 22 for the 12:00 UTC hour containing jobless claims, the Philadelphia Fed index, housing starts and building permits, and peaks at 24 for the 13:00 UTC hour holding the 13:30 UTC cash open, which is the declared danger window. That peak is conditional: it prices the possibility that the first full regular session after a policy shift establishes persistent one-way structure, not an observation that it has. Tail remains below the block threshold in every modelled hour.

lookbackSummary: Across the past 24 published hours the Claude state opened at 15 at Tuesday's 23:00 UTC hour and eased through the low band overnight, bottoming at 13 at 01:00 UTC while Asia and Europe held a contained normal range, then running 14 to 16 through the European morning. It moved to the watch band at 12:00 UTC with the U.S. pre-market and held 20 to 22 through the afternoon, briefly reading trend-up at 15:00 and 16:00 UTC. It rose to 24 at 18:00 UTC as the FOMC statement landed. The window's peak was 31 at 19:00 UTC, the only orange hour, published while the index sat at its session low during the Warsh press conference with no retracement yet formed; that reading captured the structure observed at the time and the subsequent 192-point recovery into the 28,945.06 cash close invalidated its continuation premise. The 20:00 UTC hour fell back to 20 as event/whipsaw, 21:00 published 18 during the CME maintenance halt, and 22:00 stepped down to 16 once the Globex reopen proved two-sided. All 24 hours are available, with Stress never leaving the high band.
outlookSummary: The forecast opens at 18 for the current hour, the only slot backed by observed reopen structure, and holds 16 to 18 across the Asian session with the trough at 04:00 UTC. That overnight floor sits slightly above a quiet night because the disputed Saudi pipeline repair timeline keeps a crude headline channel open, not because of any observed index structure. The path firms to 17 to 18 through the European pre-open and cash open as continental desks price the hike for the first time, then to 19 for the 11:00 UTC hour as U.S. pre-market positioning builds. It enters the watch band at 22 for the 12:00 UTC hour containing jobless claims, the Philadelphia Fed index, housing starts and building permits, four simultaneous prints in a thin pre-open tape. It peaks at 24 for the 13:00 UTC hour holding the 13:30 UTC cash open, which is the declared danger window and the highest modelled value, because the first full regular session after a policy shift is where persistent one-way structure would establish if it is going to. That peak is conditional and decays to 22 and then 20 as opening-auction structure becomes legible, returning to the low band by 16:00 UTC. A secondary rise to 20 covers the 19:00 UTC power hour, the slot that produced the lookback window's worst reading, before the 20:00 UTC cash close, the maintenance halt and the next Globex reopen return the path to 17. Tail stays below the block threshold in all 24 modelled hours and Stress remains in the high band throughout, reflecting a rates backdrop that intraday equity trade does not resolve.
